provenance.source: P1-E21-W5-S45-T3 full_desc and T0 ruling R-14.63, both quoting the same default label set
provenance.captured_by: transcribed by hand from the ruling and contract text (no tool; the set is prose in those documents)
provenance.why: Core ships NO label set (R-14.63): the labels below are the ones the cascade-pa plugin injects through its own plugin config. Recording them here as data, with the expectations they must produce, is what makes the taxonomy test a check on the mechanism against a real caller's table rather than a lookup of a literal the test itself just wrote.

expectations.label: code
expectations.why: declared in the injected set, so it resolves to its canonical topic

expectations.label: memory
expectations.why: second declared label, so one mapped row cannot pass by accident

expectations.label: CODE
expectations.why: Resolve is case-sensitive: a classifier's casing is never normalised at this layer, so a differently-cased label is simply unmapped

expectations.label: code
expectations.why: no trimming here either - Boundary.Label arrives already trimmed (segmenter_types.go), so a trailing space means the classifier produced a different label
segment zero carries no label at all (auto_thread.go), and the empty string is deliberately not a special case

expectations.label: chit-chat
expectations.why: a plausible label this caller never declared
